identification.title: Praise Adonai
identification.album: Open the Eyes of My Heart
identification.notes: Written by Paul Baloche; CCLI 2612742. Published by Integrity's Hosanna! Music, with a 1999 copyright notice on a lead sheet seen in search results and a first release in 2000 per SecondHandSongs. The list's attribution to Baloche is right. Reviewed as the song, not as any one recording.

claims.structuralNotes: One verse and one chorus, each repeated, ending on the chorus; no bridge. The verse is a rhetorical question about God's incomparability and speaks of Christ as the Lion and the Lamb on the throne, with creation bowing and roaring before the Lord of hosts, in the third person. The chorus is a call to all peoples, angels and saints to praise Adonai from morning to evening. It is exhortation to the whole creation, not personal testimony. Adonai is the Hebrew title Lord, used here of the God who is also Christ the Lamb.

claims.claim: No one is like the Lord; God is incomparable.
claims.subject: God's incomparability

claims.claim: Christ is the Lion and the Lamb, enthroned.
claims.subject: The deity and reign of Christ

claims.claim: Creation bows and roars before the Lord of hosts.
claims.subject: Creation's response to God

claims.claim: All peoples, angels and saints are summoned to praise Adonai through the day.
claims.subject: Universal call to worship

strengths.title: The Lord is incomparable
strengths.explanation: The verse asks who is like the Lord and answers by setting him above all things, so the song's praise rests on who God is.
strengths.scriptureRationale: Who is like you among the gods - the question the verse puts to the congregation.

strengths.title: Christ as Lion and Lamb on the throne
strengths.explanation: The verse names Christ as the Lion and the Lamb on the throne, joining the Lord of hosts and the Lamb in one worship.
strengths.scriptureRationale: The Lion of Judah who is also the slain Lamb, at the center of the throne.

strengths.title: A call to every people and the angels
strengths.explanation: The chorus summons all peoples, angels and saints to praise, which is a corporate and wide-reaching picture of worship.
strengths.scriptureRationale: A multitude from every nation and the angels giving praise to God and the Lamb.

doctrinesAffirmed: The deity and reign of Christ as Lion and Lamb
The worship of all peoples, angels and saints
theological.assessment: Nothing to correct. Adonai is the Hebrew title Lord, used for the God who is also Christ the Lamb. The song states no redemptive act, so the gospel is implicit rather than told, but nothing in it is false.

strengths.title: Simple and easy to learn
strengths.explanation: The melody is simple and the words are few, so a congregation can learn it at once.

strengths.title: The congregation addressed as a whole
strengths.explanation: The chorus is a summons to all peoples, angels and saints, and it puts the room into a larger company at worship.

communal.vocalRangeNote: No chart was read, so the published key is not stated here; the melody is simple.

range.note: No chart was read for this review, so the pitches are not stated.

communal.repetitionAssessment: The verse and the chorus are each repeated and the song ends on the chorus. With so little text the repeat does much of the work, though it keeps returning to a call to praise.
communal.assessment: Easy for a room to sing and shaped as a call to worship. Its short text and heavy repeat suit an opening or a gathering song.

strengths.title: Adonai and the Lion and the Lamb
strengths.explanation: The verse and chorus name Adonai, the Lord of hosts and the Lion and the Lamb, so it is clear who is praised.

clarity.assessment: Clear. Adonai may be unfamiliar to some, but it is explained by its place beside Lord of hosts and the Lion and the Lamb.

synthesis.summary: A short song of praise built on one verse and one chorus. The verse asks who is like the Lord, names Christ as the Lion and the Lamb on the throne and has creation bowing before him; the chorus calls all peoples, angels and saints to praise Adonai from morning to evening. It is third person and corporate, with no personal testimony. It states no redemptive act, so the gospel is implicit, and nothing in it is false.

scriptureReferences.relevance: Who is like the Lord - the verse's question of God's incomparability.
The Lion and the Lamb - the verse's picture of Christ enthroned.
From the rising of the sun the Lord's name is to be praised - the chorus's morning to evening.
Nations, angels and saints worshiping together - the chorus's summons.
The Lord of hosts as King of glory - the verse's title for God.
The Lord's name great among the nations - the chorus's call to all peoples.
